newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SKorea Jinro to allow bail-out to expire on Sunday.
newsitem.headline: SKorea Jinro to allow bail-out to expire on Sunday.

text.p: Creditor banks would not extend the bail-out period for South Korea's battered Jinro Group, slated for Sunday, a senior official at the Commercial Bank of Korea said on Tuesday.
"The bail-out period of Jinro Group will expire on July 27 as scheduled," said Ku Ja-yong, director and deputy president of Commercial Bank.
The bank is a major creditor of the nation's leading retailing and textile business group and 19th ranked conglomerate.
"Instead, we are planning to suggest extending the period of principal payments and reducing interest payments in order to help the group survive," he said.
Jinro's creditors are due to meet on Friday to discuss the future of the group.

The Jinro Group was tapped for rescue by a bank bail-out committee in April when creditor banks decided to keep the conglomerate afloat. But only two affiliates so far have received emergency loans from creditors as the group chairman and his family have not yet given up their management rights.
"It's almost impossible to grant additional loans to Jinro, unless they give up their management rights," Ku said.
He said Jinro could survive if financial institutions would extend the period of principal payments and cut interest payments and if the group would continue its self-rescue plan.
But analysts said the Jinro Group would default on their debts when the bail-out period expired as non-banking financial institutions were expected to call in their loan payments.
The news immediately depressed shares in Jinro Group on the Seoul bourse.
